methods.summary: Offset this match by the given amount and return a new match.

methods.name: start

methods.summary: Return a new match with the end offset replaced with the given value.

methods.name: with_start

items.summary: NoError provides an error type for matchers that never produce errors.

items.name: Captures
items.summary: A trait that describes implementations of capturing groups.

methods.name: as_match
methods.summary: Return the overall match for the capture.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Return the capturing group match at the given index. If no match of that capturing group exists, then this returns `None`.

methods.name: interpolate
methods.signature: fn interpolate<F>(&self, name_to_index: F, haystack: &[u8], replacement: &[u8], dst: &mut Vec<u8>) where F: FnMut(&str) -> Option<usize>
methods.summary: Expands all instances of `$name` in `replacement` to the corresponding capture group `name`, and writes them to the `dst` buffer given.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if these captures are empty. This occurs when `len` is `0`.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Return the total number of capturing groups. This includes capturing groups that have not matched anything.

items.name: Matcher
items.summary: A matcher defines an interface for regular expression implementations.

methods.name: capture_count
methods.summary: Returns the total number of capturing groups in this matcher.

methods.name: capture_index
methods.summary: Maps the given capture group name to its corresponding capture group index, if one exists. If one does not exist, then `None` is returned.

methods.summary: Populates the first set of capture group matches from `haystack` into `caps`. If no match exists, then `false` is returned.

methods.name: find
methods.summary: Returns the start and end byte range of the first match in `haystack`. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: find_at
methods.signature: fn find_at(&self, haystack: &[u8], at: usize) -> Result<Option<Match>, Self::Error>
methods.summary: Returns the start and end byte range of the first match in `haystack` after `at`, where the byte offsets are relative to that start of `haystack` (and not `at`). If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: find_candidate_line

methods.signature: fn find_iter<F>(&self, haystack: &[u8], matched: F) -> Result<(), Self::Error> where F: FnMut(Match) -> bool
methods.summary: Executes the given function over successive non-overlapping matches in `haystack`. If no match exists, then the given function is never called. If the function returns `false`, then iteration stops.

methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the matcher matches the given haystack starting at the given position.
